evidence.note: Runs run_tests.sh after nearly every edit, confirming both correctness and cycle count at each optimization stage — solidly above the anchor-5 'after significant changes' bar.
Correctness failures caught by the test are treated as blocking; agent halts optimization to debug rather than assuming the transform was safe.

Builds self-constructed checks: runs a smaller synthetic input (forest_height=4) and traces intermediate idx_arr state per-pc against hand-derived expected idx_addr sequences — a diff-against-reference on a self-made edge input, matching anchor 8.

Per-transform correctness isolation: disables d=2 mux to confirm d=1 still passes (1958), and compares 'without mux (2009)' vs 'with d=1 mux (1956)' to attribute both cycle effect and correctness to a single transform.

Explicitly runs several test seeds near the end to confirm correctness is maintained across randomized inputs — deliberate robustness check beyond the canonical case (though a one-off rather than systematic).

reasoning: The agent re-ran run_tests.sh (which covers randomized-seed correctness plus cycle thresholds) after virtually every semantic-affecting change and treated correctness failures as hard gates, exceeding anchor 5. Beyond the canonical test it built additional self-constructed checks — small-input tracing with intermediate-state comparison against hand-derived expected values (94-103), transform-isolation toggles (95,135), and an explicit multi-seed run (167) — which are the hallmarks of anchor 8. It does not reach anchor 10 because the reference-diffing was largely reactive debugging and the multi-seed robustness check was a single late act rather than a systematic proactive regime.
